topic: ₹2 lakh holiday: save first or take a loan?
hook_pattern: big-question (save first or EMI for a ₹2 lakh trip?)
caption:
A ₹2 lakh holiday on a loan costs more than ₹2 lakh. Saving first costs less every month.

Illustrative maths for a trip 12 months away:
Save first: ₹2,00,000 ÷ 12 = about ₹16,700 a month, and nothing extra to pay back.
Go now on a 12-month personal loan at 14% a year (personal loan rates in India currently range from about 10% to well over 30% a year): EMI of about ₹17,960, so about ₹15,500 in interest, plus any processing fee (commonly 0.5–4% of the loan).

Same trip, same 12 months of payments. One way costs about ₹1,300 a month more and leaves you paying for a holiday that's already over.

How to save for it: open a separate account or recurring deposit just for the trip, set the transfer for salary day, and book once the money is there.

Save this before you plan your next trip. Send it to your travel buddy.

Sources: published comparisons of personal loan interest rates in India (Jun and Oct 2026). EMI and rupee amounts are our illustrative calculations.
